_source: UV-A1 (docs/eras/uv.md, 'A1. Thorium' and 'Older machines, new modes'): the three thorium rows of IV's fuel fabrication plant. Real processes: ThO2 fuel for light-water and accelerator-driven cores (Shippingport, MYRRHA studies), carbothermal nitridation of an actinide oxide (ThO2 + 2 C + N2 -> ThN + 2 CO, as for uranium nitride fuel), and the U-233 rod of the thorium cycle.
_how_it_is_used: Read by server_scripts/grindless/iv/uranium_cycle.js after the steps of uranium_cycle.json; the same format (itemsIn, fluidsIn, fluidsKept, itemsOut) plus fluidsOut (the plant's type holds one). Circuits 4-6 and 13-18: 1-3 are IV's, 7-12 other fronts'. The thorium rows chain thoria (tables/thorium_refining.json) -> nitride -> pellets -> pins (15-15Ti tube + helium) -> assemblies (2 pins + 2 stainless plates; 8 thorium per assembly).

energy: plain stages, no 'from' (they are design figures, not GTM recipes): each is one IV assembler stage (1,536,000 EU, as the LEU assembly) or a multiple of it, spent at the plant's maxEUt like every row of uranium_cycle.json.

energy.stage: bundling two pins with their grids and closing the assembly: one IV assembler stage
bundling two pins with their grids and closing the assembly: one IV assembler stage
carbothermal nitridation of the thoria under 15N (ThO2 + 2 C + 1/2 N2 -> ThN + 2 CO): three IV assembler stages
pressing and sintering the nitride pellets under a 15N flush (the nitride sheds nitrogen near 2,000 C, and natural nitrogen would dilute the enrichment; the flush is lost): two IV assembler stages
pressing and sintering the thoria pellets with a niobia sintering aid (Nb2O5-doped ThO2 densifies hundreds of degrees below pure thoria; the dopant stays in the pellets): two IV assembler stages
stacking the pellets, helium-filling the tube and welding the end plugs: one IV assembler stage
stacking the pellets, helium-filling the tube and welding the end plugs: one IV assembler stage
alloying the titanium-stabilised 15Cr-15Ni steel and drawing it to tube: half an IV assembler stage
casting the metal slugs, sodium-bonding them into the tubes and closing the rod: one IV assembler stage
